entries.subject: perf(dashboard): keep getDashboardStats on indexed Postgres + index-friendly withdrawals predicate
entries.body:
EXPLAIN ANALYZE on prod proved the period-aggregate legs run 5-8ms on the
new ledger indexes (#1/#2) AND stay cent-exact with zero CDC lag, so the
money-exact headline composite serves faster + live from Postgres than the
lagging ClickHouse mirror. Removes dashboard_stats from
CUTOVER_DEFAULT_CLICKHOUSE (the CH twin + comparison wiring stay dormant for
drift checks / future Edge Config re-enable).

Also rewrites the three card_withdrawal_requests period predicates from
`COALESCE(completed_at, shipped_at) >= cutoff` to the algebraically-identical
`completed_at >= cutoff OR (completed_at IS NULL AND shipped_at >= cutoff)`,
exposing the bare completed_at column that idx_cwr_status_completed_at covers
(no semantic / money change).

entries.subject: fix(users/[id] affiliate): source click/wager from live affiliate_code_usages, widen render gate
entries.body:
The Affiliate Stats column on /users/[id] read totalReferred and
totalWagerVolumeUsd straight off the affiliate_accounts denormalized
aggregate, so code-owners whose aggregate hadn't been backfilled by the
backend rendered $0.00 even when affiliate_code_usages had the real
activity. The creator leaderboard already reads live from the same
table (creators-leaderboards.ts:142-161), so the two surfaces
disagreed for the same code.

Add a single-round-trip live aggregate keyed on UPPER(code) IN
(this user's affiliate_codes) with usage_type::text='wager' — exact
same semantics as the leaderboard — and use those values for the
two click/wager tiles. Payout state (totalEarnedUsd, availableUsd,
totalPaidOutUsd, totalBonusDistributedUsd, lastPayoutAt) stays on
affiliate_accounts because that's the authoritative cash-out source.

Widen the render gate: previously the affiliate prop was null
unless an affiliate_accounts row existed, hiding the column for
code-owners whose denormalized row hadn't been written yet. Now
returns non-null whenever the user owns at least one affiliate_code,
has any recorded usages, or has an affiliate_accounts row.

Live-verified against MAIN (read-only):
  dgentv  (DEGENTV):  12 referred / $528.02 wager (live) — was 10 / $528.02 (account)
  MrRowbee (cross-check): 167 referred / $59,091.95 wager
  kyro777 (non-affiliate): no codes/usages/account → panel does not render

entries.subject: fix(ui/dropdown-menu): forward onSelect → base-ui Menu.Item onClick at the source
entries.body:
base-ui's `Menu.Item` has no `onSelect` prop (that's a Radix-ism). The wrapper
previously spread an `onSelect` handler straight onto the element as a dead DOM
attribute that never fires on a menu-item press, so every action menu written
with `<DropdownMenuItem onSelect={...}>` was silently dead (click did nothing).

Fix it once in the shared primitive instead of per call site: accept `onSelect`
and forward it to the item's `onClick`, merging with any explicit `onClick` so
both run. base-ui's `onClick` fires on BOTH mouse press AND keyboard activation
(Enter/Space) via the composite `useButton` (verified in
@base-ui/react/use-button/useButton.js), so `onSelect` keyboard semantics are
preserved. `closeOnClick` (default true) still runs first — menu closes, then
the handler/dialog opens.

Resurrects the live previously-dead onSelect call sites at once:
- creators/_components/creator-row-actions.tsx (Revoke creator role)
- withdrawals/row-actions.tsx ActiveShipmentActions (Mark Shipped / Complete /
  Cancel / Mark Failed) — fixed at source; that component is not currently
  mounted by the /withdrawals table, so it's covered by tsc + next build only.

Existing onClick menus are untouched (onClick is destructured and forwarded
unchanged) — admin-users row + roles kebabs, packs, employees, theme switcher.

Browser-verified (minted-session Playwright, logged-in):
- /creators "Revoke creator role" (real onSelect) opens its confirm dialog on
  mouse click AND keyboard Enter — the bug, now fixed; no console errors.
- /admin-users "Edit roles" (onClick) + roles-tab Rename (onClick) still open
  their dialogs — no regression on already-working menus.

delete. (`onSelect` is a Radix-ism; base-ui uses `onClick`.)

mutation so the list reflects the change without a manual reload.

The list calls the same guarded server actions (toggleAdminActive /
deleteAdminUser), so every safety guard is unchanged: last-admin protection,
self-deactivate/self-delete block, session revocation, 2FA, and audit events.

Verified (Playwright + minted admin session): both dialogs open from the list
row; confirming with an invalid 2FA code reaches the action and the guard fires;
the signed-in admin's own Deactivate/Delete are disabled. No regression to the

that swallowed the real exception. The prior incident root cause was a

DB that had renamed the column to shards) — invisible from the client.

Add classifyAdjustBalanceError(): the unexpected-error path now logs the
full exception server-side (unchanged) AND returns a SAFE, category-
distinguishing client message — explicitly naming the P2022 schema-mismatch
case ("a column the admin expects is missing on the live DB; needs a
code/schema fix, not a retry") and other Prisma DB errors by code — without
leaking the connection string, query text, or stack. Business errors
(negative balance, concurrent version) still surface verbatim.

Read-only reconciliation of the live prod game DB confirmed balances +
ledger_transactions have no remaining drift for this write (all required
NOT-NULL columns supplied, ledger type/status enums present), so the
already-shipped bonus_points model removal (e9932d4f) fixes the throw;
this change makes any future recurrence diagnosable from the toast alone.

entries.subject: fix(users/[id]): balance adjustments failing — drop dead balances.bonus_points from Prisma mirror

The game DB renamed balances.bonus_points -> shards, but the admin's Prisma
`balances` model still declared bonus_points. Every `balances` findUnique-all
(no select) — including the one inside adjustBalance()'s transaction — emitted
`SELECT ... bonus_points ... FROM balances`, which 42703'd on prod and surfaced
as the generic "Balance adjustment failed — please try again". The user-detail
page rendered fine because it reads balances via a selective/raw-SQL query
(fetchBalancePoints already probes bonus_points vs shards), so ONLY the
findUnique-all path (balance adjustments) broke.

on the live game DB. No code reads model.bonus_points (the "Bonus Points" UI
value comes from the raw column probe, not this field). Read-only verified the
